_README: EXAMPLE capability manifest. Copy it, replace the tools, keep the shape.
Cohaera's default classifier guesses what a tool does from its NAME. That
guess has been wrong in both directions in every review round so far:
budget_report read as read_only because 'get' is inside 'budget';
postmortem_read read as egress because 'post' is inside 'postmortem'.
Whole-token matching fixed those. It cannot fix the general case, because
sync_to_partner is egress and sync_local_cache is not, and no amount of
tokenising separates them.
A manifest replaces the guess with a declaration, keyed on the EXACT tool
ID the producer emits in tool_name. Tools not listed here fall back to the
heuristic and DEGRADE that session's coverage confidence, which is the
intended pressure: the score tells you how much of the verdict rests on
guesswork.
Precedence, highest first:
1. this manifest, matched on exact tool_id
2. egress by name
3. the producer's per-call 'reversible' flag
4. the name heuristic
The manifest outranks 'reversible' deliberately. That flag arrives on the
event, in band, from the same path an attacker would use to hide an action.
This file is loaded out of band from a path the operator chose.
SIGNING IS AVAILABLE AND UNSIGNED IS STILL THE DEFAULT. This file can
carry a detached cohaera.policy_signature:1 signature, minted by
tools/policy_sign.py with a key holding the 'policy' role and supplied
with --tool-manifest-sig. A run given one that does not verify REFUSES to
score; a run given none records POLICY_SIGNATURE_ABSENT, which is the
value nearly every deployment will carry and is recorded rather than
left to be assumed.
What a signature establishes is narrow: these are the bytes the holder of
that key approved. It says nothing about whether the declarations in them
are right. Cohaera records TWO SHA-256 digests of this file in every
verdict's provenance block either way, so two runs that disagree about
what a tool does are distinguishable after the fact.
file_digest      over the exact bytes. Moves for ANY edit, including a
reformat and including a field Cohaera does not read.
semantic_digest  over the declarations Cohaera parsed out. Moves only
when the meaning changes. Reformat this file and it
stays put; change an effect and it does not.
Same semantic_digest, different file_digest: the policy did not change.
Different semantic_digest: it did, and verdicts on either side of the edit
are answering different questions.
Usage: cohaera score run.jsonl --tool-manifest this_file.json
THE 'policies' SECTION AT THE BOTTOM IS OPTIONAL, and the reason it
exists is worth reading before you skip it.
CH04 asks whether consequential work continued after a guardrail fired.
Whether that is a BYPASS depends on whether the guardrail was supposed
to stop anything, and a policy engine can declare that on the event
itself as an 'enforcement' field.
Declaring it on the event means believing the thing being watched. Note
the asymmetry, because it decides how much that matters: a producer
cannot MANUFACTURE a bypass finding by declaring 'blocking' -- that only
makes Cohaera louder about the producer's own behaviour -- but it CAN
suppress one entirely by declaring 'advisory'. One string, and the check
whose job is to notice a circumvention goes quiet. That is EVASION.md
E20, and it is the same shape as the in-band 'reversible' flag deciding
whether a call is consequential.
So a declaration here OUTRANKS the event, with the same precedence and
for the same reason a tool capability outranks 'reversible': the
operator chose this file, the agent wrote the event.
Key on the producer's policy_id where it emits one, and on the EVENT
TYPE otherwise -- observra's cost_threshold_exceeded and depth_exceeded
carry no policy identifier at all.
Where nothing declares a policy, CH04 keeps its old behaviour and its
old check ID: it reports the sequence, claims no bypass, and coverage
says POLICY_SEMANTICS_UNDECLARED.
There is a second reason to fill this section in, and it applies to the
sessions where NOTHING fires. A session with no policy event is either
a governed agent that stayed inside its limits or an agent with no
limits at all, and the event stream cannot tell those apart -- both are
an absence. This section can: it says the controls exist. With it, a
quiet session means CH04 looked and found nothing, and CH04 reports
evaluated. Without it, CH04 declines with NO_POLICY_EVIDENCE, because
a clean verdict over evidence it never had is the worst output this
project can produce.

draft_reply._note: Drafting produces no external effect. Sending does.

budget_report._note: The heuristic read this as read_only for the WRONG reason ('get' inside 'budget'). Right answer, wrong evidence. A declaration makes it right for the right reason.

postmortem_read._note: The heuristic classified this as egress ('post' inside 'postmortem') until whole-token matching landed.

sync_local_cache._note: The heuristic still calls this egress because 'sync' is an egress keyword. It is not. This entry is why exact IDs beat token matching.

sync_to_partner._note: Same verb as sync_local_cache, opposite trust boundary. No lexical rule separates these two.

cost_threshold_exceeded.description: Soft budget alert. The agent is expected to continue; finance reconciles later. Declared here so CH04 stops paging on correct behaviour.

depth_exceeded.description: Delegation depth is a hard ceiling. Consequential work after this, with no bound cohaera.approval:1 covering it, is a bypass and Cohaera will say so.

external-data-egress.description: Keyed on policy_id rather than event type, which is what a real policy engine emits. Paired with sync_to_partner above.
